The petitioner has filed this claim petition U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act, 1989, against the respondents seeking compensation on account of death of one Sri.Narasimhappa, in the Motor Vehicle Accident.
02.

The brief facts of the case of the petitioners is as under:
(SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.5635/2023

That on 07.11.2015 at about 08.00 p.m, when the husband of petitioner Narasimhappa was crossing road near Kurubarahalli Gate, on Chikkaballapura - Manchenalli Main Road, the driver of respondent No.1 vehicle bearing No.KA-40-G-213 came in rash and negligent manner and dashed against said Narasimhappa.

Due to which he sustained grievous injuries and immediately after the accident he was shifted to General hospital,
Gowribidanur, but he was declared as dead.
Prior to the accident the deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 50 years and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.

Due to untimely death of the deceased,
the petitioner lost her loving husband who is only bread earning member of the family and undergoing lost of pain and agony at this old age.

The accident is occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending Ambulance and in this regard the Gowribidanur Police have registered a case against driver of the offending Ambulance.

The petitioner herein is uneducated and residing at village, having no worldly knowledge and now known about entitlement of compensation out of the accident and one of the relative assured that he will help out in getting compenstion amount from 108 (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.5635/2023 ambulance side, but as on today no such compensation was given to them and on enquiry it is learnt that the said relative has not filed any petition before this court or before any other court in seeking compensation.

Due to lack of knowledge and above said bonafide reasons, there is delay in filing the claim petition by the petitioner and hence said delay may be condoned by appreciating the above said facts and circumstances.

The respondent No.1 is the RC Owner, respondent No.2 being the driver and respondent No.3 is the insurer of the said offending ambulance vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- to the petitioners with cost and interest at the rate of 18% p.a.
03.
Inspite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 did not appeared and hence was placed exparte.
On service of notice, the respondents No.2 and 3 have appeared before the tribunal through their counsels and have filed objections.

sentences.text: The respondent No.2 in his objections has denied the entire case of the petitioner and further denied the alleged accident, negligence of the driver of offending ambulance, name, age, avocation and income of the deceased, dependency of the petitioner (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.5635/2023 and nature of the injuries sustained by the deceased and treatment taken by the deceased and expenses incurred by the petitioner.

The compensation claimed is highly exaggerated, excessive and petition is bad for non-joinder and mis-joinder of necessary parties and the accident occurred on 07.11.2015 and the petition is filed on 2023 after 8 years, the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation.

The vehicle bearing No.KA-40-G-213 was not involved in the alleged accident nor caused any accident to the deceased and hence, pray to dismiss the petition with costs against respondent No.2.
05.

The respondent No.3 in its objections has denied the entire case of the petitioner and further denied the alleged accident, negligence of the driver of offending ambulance, name, age, avocation and income of the deceased and nature of the injuries sustained by the deceased, dependency of the petitioner and treatment taken by the deceased and expenses incurred by the petitioner and further denies issuance of policy of insurance in favour of respondent No.1 in respect of vehicle bearing No.KA-40-G-213 and the liability of this respondent, if any, is limited to terms and conditions of the policy and contended that (SCCH-3) 6 M.V.C.No.5635/2023 driver is a necessary party to decide issue of negligence and the deceased had ventured to cross the road abruptly without following the vehicular movements crossing as such the accident was on account of sole negligence on the part of the deceased, but the jurisdiction Police have filed Charge sheet against driver of ambulance and there is inordinate delay in filing the claim petition and the vehicle is used as ambulance for transporting the injured is not without the knowledge of this respondent and the same is in violation of policy terms and conditions regarding the conditions of use and the compensation claimed is exorbitant and hence, pray to dismiss the petition with costs against respondent No.3.
06.

Based on the aforesaid pleadings, the following issues have been framed by my learned predecessor: -
ISSUES 01. Whether petitioners prove that they are the LRs/dependents of deceased Sri.Narasimhappa S/o Chikkappaiah?
02.

Whether petitioner prove that deceased Sri.Narasimhappa S/o Chikkappaiah was died in RTA arising out of the accident alleged to have been taken place on 07.11.2015 at about 8.00 p.m, near Kurubarahalli Gate, on (SCCH-3) 7 M.V.C.No.5635/2023 Chikkaballapuramanchenahalli Main Road, due to rash and negligent driving of 108 Ambulance bearing registration No. KA-40-G-213 by its driver as alleged in the petition?
03.
Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount & from whom?
04 . What order or award?

14. Issue No.3:- This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the death of the deceased Narasimhappa, who died in the Motor Vehicle Accident.
The PW.1/petitioner has stated in her petition and chief-examination that prior to accident deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 50 years and earning Rs.6,000/- p.m as daily wage labour.
Due to untimely death of the deceased, the petitioner lost her loving husband who is only bread earning member of the family and undergoing lost of pain and agony at this old age.
15. It is the duty of the petitioners to prove age of the deceased as on the date of accident.
The petitioner has not produced any birth certificate, school records of the deceased to show his exact date of birth.
However, she has produced Aadhaar card of the deceased as per Ex.P.8.

Eventhough the said document is not authenticated document for the proof of age of any person, but in the absence of other evidence, said document can be relied upon and according to which his birth year is mentioned as (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.5635/2023 1963.
The alleged accident occurred on 07.11.2015 and hence it appears that as on the date of accident the age of the deceased is 52 years.

Therefore,
this tribunal has assessed the age of the deceased as 52 years as on the date of accident.

As per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and Ors. V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and Ors. case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 51 to 55 years is "11".
